purpose: Source-vs-declared-target physical type/default/nullability discrepancy screening only; not runtime mismatch or historical data migration evidence.
interpretation: MySQL VARCHAR vs normalized E.164/postal code intentionally differ; shorter capacity alone is not a bug without workflow proof.
MySQL nullable legacy field tightened to not-null in greenfield is often correct, but requires a creation/validation contract.
Legacy DEFAULT NULL is equivalent to no SQL default on a nullable target; do not flag as missing default.
INT key to UUID is intentional normalized greenfield design; no legacy record migration is needed.
Timestamp without timezone vs timestamptz must be verified for deadlines/cross-timezone behavior.
A Boolean soft-delete mapped to archived_at timestamp is a lifecycle redesign, not a like-for-like nullable conversion.
Passing this static report does not mean physical migrations replay, live target DB exists, or any field semantic parity is proved.

Five nontrivial type-family redesign mappings (including faculty.department free-text to UUID, boolean deletion to timestamp/status) need exact business semantics; physical target presence alone cannot close them.
